+        and url.host == other.host

item.text:
No runtime regression found in the diff. The main compatibility risk is an `ImportError` for downstream code that imports `same_origin`, `is_https_redirect`, or `port_or_default` from the private [`httpx/_utils.py`](<work>/pr3389-base/httpx/_utils.py). There are no remaining in-repo references to those names.

- **What changed.** The three helpers moved into `httpx/_client.py`, gained leading underscores, and kept the same logic. `BaseClient._redirect_headers` still rewrites `Host` on origin changes and strips `Authorization` except for same-host HTTP port 80 to HTTPS port 443 upgrades. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/pr3389-base/httpx/_client.py:545)
- **Affected callers.** `Client` and `AsyncClient` both call `_build_redirect_request`, which uses `_redirect_headers` for followed redirects and for `Response.next_request` when redirects are disabled. Top-level helpers such as `httpx.get()` and `httpx.stream()` use the same path through `Client`. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/pr3389-base/httpx/_client.py:474) · [httpx/_api.py](<work>/pr3389-base/httpx/_api.py:39)
- **Test gap.** Five existing tests moved unchanged from `tests/test_utils.py` to `tests/client/test_headers.py`. The two origin tests use the same normalized `Host` value on both sides, so they can pass whether the header is preserved or rewritten. [tests/client/test_headers.py](<work>/pr3389-base/tests/client/test_headers.py:240)

The test run could not start because the available Python interpreter lacked `pytest`.
